significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that unsupervised reaction transformers encode directional electron flow, use it causally in product prediction, and exhibit a predictive coupling whereby "the strength/consistency of the internal electron-flow representation predicts, per reaction, when the model produces mass-balanced correct products versus hallucinations"; this combines a form-(ii) causal mechanism with a form-(iii) relation between measurable representation strength and failures. It would establish both a mechanistic decomposition—donors, acceptors, and bond-electron changes—and a behavioral phenomenon that constrains which reactions should fail, materially informing whether standard reaction predictors need mechanism-explicit replacements such as ELECTRO or FlowER rather than merely adding another decodable chemistry feature. The component hypotheses are determinate, and a verified-negative result would rule out this internal-mechanism explanation for the specified transformer class and support treating its apparent chemical competence as recipe-level correlation, although mixed outcomes across decodability, causality, and prediction would weaken the claimed dichotomy. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the generic topic would suggest probing whether scientific mechanisms are represented, whereas the directional causal decomposition and representation-strength/failure coupling are specific, above-median constraints supplied by this claim.

reach.justification: The principal transferable handle is the explicitly named per-reaction "electron-flow strength," supplemented by "electron-source or bond-breaking directions" as interventions; the former is intended to predict hallucination and OOD accuracy, giving an ex-ante screening or gating signal before a predicted reaction is trusted in synthesis planning. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive conclusion predicts a relation—stronger, more conservation-consistent electron-flow representations should accompany correct and OOD-generalizing products—rather than merely supplying an open-ended procedure for finding an arbitrary direction. The asserted scope covers standard USPTO-trained reactant-to-product transformers, specifically Molecular Transformer and Chemformer, and its downstream users include researchers and practitioners deciding "whether to trust, probe, or replace standard reaction transformers," though it does not yet claim transfer to unrelated architectures, modalities, or scientific mechanisms. The topic-substitution check lowers no credit here because the reusable failure predictor and mechanism-aligned intervention disappear when the electron-flow hypothesis is deleted; the broad scientific-representation topic alone would not provide either handle.
